personality_one_liner: A deeply intimate, distraction-free space for two, pairing the highly functional clarity of iOS messaging with a warm, romantic, and inviting aesthetic.

spacing.rule: Generous vertical breathing room. Avoid dense clusters; use iOS-native spacing rhythm for comfortable touch targets and clear grouping.

do's: Use frosted glass on the bottom tab bar, especially as chat or calendar content scrolls behind it.
Use frosted glass on sticky dates/headers in the chat or calendar views.
Use blur on modal scrims when opening the 'Worries' space to separate it emotionally and visually.
dont's: Do not use glassmorphism on individual chat bubbles or form inputs.
Do not apply glass effects in dense settings views where clarity is prioritized.

screens.name: Pairing / Onboarding
screens.purpose: A warm, full-screen introductory flow explaining the private, two-person nature of the app and prompting for the invite code.

states.error: Readable inline error message for invalid invite code with retry button.

screens.layout: Hero image at the top with a top-to-bottom vertical gradient scrim, overlaid with the bold red '2Gether' logo. Below the image: title, warm supportive subtitle, and a single-column clean form for the invite code. Sticky primary CTA at the bottom inside KeyboardAvoidingView.

screens.name: Chat (Main 1-to-1 Feed)
screens.purpose: The core communication hub featuring encrypted messages, photo/video sharing with view-once toggles, and call shortcuts.

states.empty: A romantic, tinted illustration (brandTertiary container) in the center with a prompt 'Start your conversation...' and a primary button to send a photo or message.
states.error: Error banner at the top of the chat list, prompting network retry.

screens.layout: iOS-native chat structure. Sticky top header (glassmorphism) with partner's avatar, connection status, and call buttons. Scrollable chat feed with clear right/left bubble alignment. Partner bubbles in surfaceSecondary, user bubbles in brandPrimary. Sticky input composer at the bottom with a 'Worries' quick-action or media attachment icon.

screens.name: Shared Calendar
screens.purpose: A unified view of both partners' schedules, highlighting shared dates, reminders, and synced events.

states.empty: Illustration of a calendar with a heart badge, text 'No plans yet. Schedule a date night!' and a CTA to add an event.
states.error: Failed to sync calendar message with a retry button.

screens.layout: Monthly calendar widget at the top (or weekly strip), followed by a vertical, time-grouped list of upcoming events. Events use brandTertiary tags to highlight 'Shared/Date Night' vs personal tasks. Pinned action button (FAB) for adding new events.

screens.name: Worries Space
screens.purpose: A dedicated, calm conversation area to raise relationship concerns constructively without turning them into immediate chat arguments.

states.empty: Soft, calm icon layout with text 'A safe space to share what's on your mind. Everything is okay.'
states.error: Failed to load space, tap to retry.

screens.layout: Visually distinct from the main chat to signify a shift in tone. Uses a slightly warmer background (surfaceSecondary) full bleed. Card-based list of 'Topics' or 'Concerns' rather than an immediate raw chat feed, encouraging thoughtful long-form writing. Uses bottom sheet for drafting a new concern.

onboarding_hero.alt: shallow focus photography of man and woman holding hands

worries_empty_state.alt: Anonymous loving couple resting on bench while holding hands

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly adhere to the '1 iOS-Native Clean' spacing scale. Do not clutter the screen; the messaging UI should frame the conversation, not distract from it.

Implement the 'Warm Romantic Palette' meticulously: base colors are warm bone-white and soft blush/cream (no harsh pure white or cold grays), offset by the bold red 'brandPrimary' (#D92525) for buttons and user chat bubbles.
BANNED: Any shade of blue, purple, indigo, or orange. Use the provided warm charcoal (#2B2524) for primary text, and moss green / warm mustard strictly for status colors.

For the 'Worries Space', ensure a distinct tone by using `surfaceSecondary` as the main background and card-based topic threads instead of standard chat bubbles, promoting slow, thoughtful communication.
Whenever overlaying text on the onboarding hero image, you MUST implement a gradient-to-dark scrim (top to bottom, transparent to ≥70% surfaceInverse) to guarantee WCAG contrast.
All interactive elements (tabs, primary buttons, message sends) must be wired with haptic feedback (expo-haptics) to provide a tactile, responsive feel.
